items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make Voting
Easy Act" to require that the board of elections designate at least one early
voting polling place for every full increment of twenty-five thousand
registered voters in each county
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4306

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make
Voting Easy Act" to require that the board of elections designate at
least one early voting polling place for every full increment of twen-
ty-five thousand registered voters in each county

 
PURPOSE:

To require the board of elections to designate at least one early voting
polling place for every full increment of twenty-five thousand regis-
tered voters in each county.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one is the title.

Section two of the bill amends the election law by amending subdivision
2 of section 8-600 to require that the Board of Elections establish at
least one early voting polling place per 25,000 registered voters with
no maximum number of polling places.

Section three of the bill amends paragraph (c) of subdivision 4 of
section 8600 of the election law to increase the number of hours early
voting polls must be open on weekends and legal holidays from five hours
to eight hours, and requires that early voting polls on those days must
be open between nine o'clock in the morning and eight o'clock in the
evening.

Section three sets the effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

After we succeeded in establishing Early Voting in 2019, long lines and
extraordinarily long wait times for early voters in the 2020 Presiden-
tial election demonstrated that the process must be improved.  The
lengthy wait times were the result of too few polling places for the
number of registered voters and limited hours. Reducing overcrowding and
long lines at the polls is especially important in the midst of the
COVID-19 pandemic, though a fast and easy early voting experience should
be the standard for any election. Under this proposal, a majority of
counties would see an increase in the number of polling locations, and
an increase in the number of early voting poll hours on weekends and
legal holidays. Increasing the minimum number of poll sites and hours on
weekends will better facilitate Early Voting across New York State.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: Died in Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: Click here

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately and shall apply to any general, primary, run-off primary, or
special election held thereafter.

AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make Voting

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4306A

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make
Voting Easy Act" to require that the board of elections designate at
least one early voting polling place for every full increment of thir-
ty-five thousand registered voters in each county and to expand polling
site hours of operation during early voting

 
PURPOSE:

To require the board of elections to designate at least one early voting
polling place for every full increment of thirty-five thousand regis-
tered voters in each county, and to extend voting polling site hours of
operation during early voting.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one is the title.

Section two of the bill amends the election law by amending subdivision
2 of section 8-600 to require that the Board of Elections establish at
least one early voting polling place per 35,000 registered voters with
no maximum number of polling places.

Section three of the bill amends paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) of subdi-
vision 4 of section 8-600 of the election law. Paragraph (a) is amended
to read that early voting polls must be open at least eight hours per
weekday between 7AM and 9PM. Paragraph (b) is amended to read that at
least one early voting polling place must be open until 9PM on at least
3 weekdays in a calendar week. If polling places for early voting are
limited to voters from certain areas pursuant to subdivision three of
this section, polling places that remain open until 9PM shall be desig-
nated such that any person entitled to early vote may vote until 9PM at
least 3 weekdays during early voting.  Paragraph (c) is amended to
increase the number of hours early voting polls must be open on weekends
and legal holidays from five hours to ten hours on those days, and that
polls must be open for those ten hours between 9AM and 9PM.

Section three sets the effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

After we succeeded in establishing Early Voting in 2019, long lines and
extraordinarily long wait times for early voters in the 2020 Presiden-
tial election demonstrated that the process must be improved.  The
lengthy wait times were the result of too few polling places for the
number of registered voters and limited hours. Reducing overcrowding and
long lines at the polls is especially important in the midst of the
COVID-19 pandemic, though a fast and easy early voting experience should
be the standard for any election. Under this proposal, a majority of
counties would see an increase in the number of polling locations, and
an increase in the number of early voting poll hours. Increasing the
minimum number of poll sites and hours will better facilitate Early
Voting across New York State.
 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: Died in Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately and shall apply to any general, primary, run-off primary, or
special election held thereafter.

B.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make Voting
Easy Act" to require that the board of elections designate a number of early
voting polling places based on the number of registered voters in each county
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4306B

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to enacting the "Make
Voting Easy Act" to require that the board of elections designate a
number of early voting polling places based on the number of registered
voters in each county

 
PURPOSE:

To require the board of elections to designate at least one early voting
polling place for every full increment of forty thousand registered
voters in each county with at least five hundred thousand registered
voters, and for every full increment of thirty thousand registered
voters in each county with less than five hundred thousand registered
voters, and to extend voting polling site hours of operation during
early voting.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill contains the short title.

Section two amends subdivision 2 of Election Law § 8-600 to require that
the largest city in a county or, if there is no city in the county, the
largest municipality in the county, shall have at least one early voting
poll site in the city or municipality.

Section two also requires that each county with at least five hundred
thousand registered voters must have at least one early voting poll site
per 40,000 registered voters with no maximum number of polling places;
and that each county with under five hundred thousand registered voters
must have at least one early voting poll site per 30,000 registered
voters with a cap of 10 poll sites required in such counties with less
than five hundred thousand registered voters.

Section three amends paragraph (c) of subdivision 4 of Election Law §
8-600 to increase the number of hours early voting polls must be open on
weekends and legal holidays from five hours to eight hours on those
days, and that polls must be open for those eight hours between 9AM and
8PM.

Section four sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

After we succeeded in establishing early voting in 2019, long lines and
extraordinarily long wait times for early voters in the 2020 Presiden-
tial election demonstrated that the process must be improved.  The
lengthy wait times were the result of too few polling places for the
number of registered voters and the limited hours. Reducing overcrowding
and long lines at the polls is especially important during the COVID-19
pandemic, though a fast and easy early voting experience should be the
standard for any election. Under this proposal, most counties would see
an increase in the number of polling locations, and an increase in the
number of early voting poll hours. Increasing the minimum number of poll
sites and hours will better facilitate early voting across New York
State.
 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined during the adoption of the budget for fiscal year
2022-2023 when this bill takes effect.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect April 1, 2022 and shall apply to any general,
primary, run-off primary, or special election held thereafter.

summary: Enacts the "Make Voting Easy Act"; requires the board of elections to designate a number of early voting polling places based on the number of registered voters in each county; relates to the hours polls are open for early voting.
